questions.question_text: An asymmetric triangle figure starts at 0° and turns 45° clockwise each step. Select the next orientation.
questions.explanation: The figure turns 45° clockwise at every step. Applying the same rotation once more gives option B.

questions.question_text: An asymmetric diamond figure starts at 15° and turns 90° clockwise each step. Select the next orientation.
questions.explanation: The figure turns 90° clockwise at every step. Applying the same rotation once more gives option D.

questions.question_text: An asymmetric pentagon figure starts at 30° and turns 135° clockwise each step. Select the next orientation.
questions.explanation: The figure turns 135° clockwise at every step. Applying the same rotation once more gives option A.

questions.question_text: A diamond starts with 1 red dots and gains 1 dot(s) at each step. Choose the next figure.
questions.explanation: The number of marks increases by 1 each time: 1, 2, 3. The next has 4 marks (option D).

questions.question_text: A pentagon starts with 2 red dots and gains 2 dot(s) at each step. Choose the next figure.
questions.explanation: The number of marks increases by 2 each time: 2, 4, 6. The next has 8 marks (option D).

questions.question_text: A arrow starts with 3 red dots and gains 1 dot(s) at each step. Choose the next figure.
questions.explanation: The number of marks increases by 1 each time: 3, 4, 5. The next has 6 marks (option A).

questions.question_text: A L alternates filled/unfilled shading and line/dot marks, beginning at rotation 0°. Select the next state.
questions.explanation: Shading and the internal mark both alternate. After filled-with-line, unfilled-with-dot is required (option B).

questions.question_text: A L alternates filled/unfilled shading and line/dot marks, beginning at rotation 23°. Select the next state.
questions.explanation: Shading and the internal mark both alternate. After filled-with-line, unfilled-with-dot is required (option A).

questions.question_text: A L alternates filled/unfilled shading and line/dot marks, beginning at rotation 46°. Select the next state.
questions.explanation: Shading and the internal mark both alternate. After filled-with-line, unfilled-with-dot is required (option C).

questions.question_text: Complete the 2×2 L matrix with a 45° row rotation and changing internal mark.
questions.explanation: Across each row, orientation advances by 45° and the internal mark changes dot→line. Down the second column, shading changes to filled. The missing figure is option A.

questions.question_text: Complete the 2×2 L matrix with a 90° row rotation and changing internal mark.
questions.explanation: Across each row, orientation advances by 90° and the internal mark changes dot→line. Down the second column, shading changes to filled. The missing figure is option C.

questions.question_text: Complete the 2×2 L matrix with a 135° row rotation and changing internal mark.
questions.explanation: Across each row, orientation advances by 135° and the internal mark changes dot→line. Down the second column, shading changes to filled. The missing figure is option B.

questions.question_text: Choose the vertical mirror of the asymmetric L at orientation 13°, preserving its dot.
questions.explanation: Reflect the figure across the vertical axis; the shape's orientation reverses while the internal mark remains unchanged. Option B matches.

questions.question_text: Choose the water image of the asymmetric L at orientation 42°, preserving its line.
questions.explanation: Reflect the figure across the horizontal axis; the shape's orientation reverses while the internal mark remains unchanged. Option A matches.

questions.question_text: Choose the vertical mirror of the asymmetric L at orientation 71°, preserving its dot.
questions.explanation: Reflect the figure across the vertical axis; the shape's orientation reverses while the internal mark remains unchanged. Option A matches.

questions.question_text: A square is folded once along its vertical centre line; punches lie near the top and near the bottom on the folded half. Choose its unfolded pattern.
questions.explanation: Unfolding reflects every punch across the fold line. Each punch therefore appears with its mirror counterpart at equal distance on the opposite half. Option B shows all reflected positions.

questions.question_text: A square is folded once along its vertical centre line; punches lie at the upper-middle and at the lower-middle on the folded half. Choose its unfolded pattern.
questions.explanation: Unfolding reflects every punch across the fold line. Each punch therefore appears with its mirror counterpart at equal distance on the opposite half. Option A shows all reflected positions.

questions.question_text: A square is folded once along its vertical centre line; punches lie at the centre and at the centre on the folded half. Choose its unfolded pattern.
questions.explanation: Unfolding reflects every punch across the fold line. Each punch therefore appears with its mirror counterpart at equal distance on the opposite half. Option C shows all reflected positions.

questions.question_text: Figure A changes to B by a 45° rotation. Apply the same transformation to figure C.
questions.explanation: A→B rotates the complete figure clockwise by 45° without changing fill or its internal mark. Applying that same turn to C gives option A.

questions.question_text: Figure A changes to B by a 90° rotation. Apply the same transformation to figure C.
questions.explanation: A→B rotates the complete figure clockwise by 90° without changing fill or its internal mark. Applying that same turn to C gives option C.

questions.question_text: Figure A changes to B by a 135° rotation. Apply the same transformation to figure C.
questions.explanation: A→B rotates the complete figure clockwise by 135° without changing fill or its internal mark. Applying that same turn to C gives option B.

questions.question_text: Among the triangle, diamond, pentagon, arrow figures, three share the central dot property. Select the figure that does not share it.
questions.explanation: Options A, B, D share the central dot property. Option C differs in that property, so C is the unique odd figure.

questions.question_text: Among the diamond, pentagon, arrow, L figures, three share the filled interior property. Select the figure that does not share it.
questions.explanation: Options A, B, D share the filled interior property. Option C differs in that property, so C is the unique odd figure.

questions.question_text: Among the pentagon, arrow, L, triangle figures, three share the central dot property. Select the figure that does not share it.
questions.explanation: Options A, B, C share the central dot property. Option D differs in that property, so D is the unique odd figure.

questions.question_text: Find the option containing a square with the rising diagonal, in the same orientation.
questions.explanation: Only option D contains all four square sides and the target's rising diagonal. The other panels either reverse/omit a diagonal, add a different internal line or change the square proportions.

questions.question_text: Find the option containing a square with the falling diagonal, in the same orientation.
questions.explanation: Only option B contains all four square sides and the target's falling diagonal. The other panels either reverse/omit a diagonal, add a different internal line or change the square proportions.

questions.question_text: Find the option containing a square with the both diagonals, in the same orientation.
questions.explanation: Only option C contains all four square sides and the target's both diagonals. The other panels either reverse/omit a diagonal, add a different internal line or change the square proportions.

questions.question_text: Count all triangles in the figure with 2 internal horizontal levels, including composite triangles.
questions.explanation: Each internal horizontal segment and the outside base form one triangle with the apex. Thus 2 internal levels make 2+1=3 triangles; option D.

questions.question_text: Count all triangles in the figure with 3 internal horizontal levels, including composite triangles.
questions.explanation: Each internal horizontal segment and the outside base form one triangle with the apex. Thus 3 internal levels make 3+1=4 triangles; option C.

questions.question_text: Count all triangles in the figure with 4 internal horizontal levels, including composite triangles.
questions.explanation: Each internal horizontal segment and the outside base form one triangle with the apex. Thus 4 internal levels make 4+1=5 triangles; option D.

questions.question_text: Choose the figure with the red dot inside the circle and outside the square (diagram 1).
questions.explanation: Option B lies inside the circle but beyond the square edge.

questions.question_text: Choose the figure with the red dot inside the circle and outside the triangle (diagram 2).
questions.explanation: Option A lies inside the circle but outside the triangle; D and C lie in the triangle and B is outside the circle.

questions.question_text: Choose the figure with the red dot inside the overlap of both circles (diagram 3).
questions.explanation: Option D lies in both circles. A and B lie in only one circle, while C lies outside both.
